sections.h2: Where is the Webster County Recorder of Deeds?
sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds works from Room 16 of the Webster County Courthouse in Marshfield. The Recorder's own page gives the street as 101 N Crittenden, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 546, Marshfield, MO 65706, and the phone is 417-859-5882. Other county pages print the courthouse as 101 S Crittenden, so call before you mail anything or drive in.

Stacy Atkison is the elected Recorder, and Sarah Bodine serves as Deputy Recorder. The office's stated mission is to record and preserve land records accurately and quickly. It also issues marriage licenses and records and copies military discharge papers (DD-214).

Marshfield sits 1,490 feet above sea level and is the highest county seat in Missouri. The present courthouse, faced in Carthage marble, was built from 1939 to 1941 and is the county's third.

Marshfield itself was laid out in 1856 on land given by C.F. Dryden and W.T. and B.F.T. Burford. Until a courthouse was built, county business was conducted at Hazelwood, where Joseph W. McClurg, later a governor of Missouri, ran a general store.

sections.h2: How much does Webster County charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
A standard document is $26 for page one and $3 for every page after that, according to the Recorder's page. Documents that miss the format rules carry a $25 penalty on top. Copies of recorded documents are $1.00 per page.

One caution about timing. Missouri raised recorder fees by a flat $2.00 on August 28, 2026 under Senate Bill 938, a change the Stone County Recorder announced and that appears in the amended text of RSMo 59.319. Ask the Webster office whether the $26 price on its page already includes that increase.

sections.h2: What layout does a Webster County deed have to follow?
sections.html:
Webster County lists three layout standards: a three inch margin at the top of the first page, three-quarters of an inch on the remaining sides, and letter-size white paper. A deed outside those lines is treated as non-standard and costs the extra $25.

State law adds content requirements. Under RSMo 59.330, a deed has to carry a legal description of the land and a mailing address for one grantee, and the Recorder may not file it without them. Closing agents normally prepare the deed with these items in place, but a seller preparing a deed without a title company should check each one before mailing it.

sections.h2: How do you search Webster County land records online?
sections.html:
The Recorder's online document search went live on February 1, 2023. The site is titled Document Search for the Index of Recorded Deeds. A visitor registers as a new user, and the account can then search and buy copies of recorded documents. Subscription levels run from free to several paid options, depending on use.

Searching in person at the Recorder's office in Room 16 is free to the public. The county's page for the service gives the paid online plan as $200 per month, with a limit of 300 documents viewed or printed. An owner checking a single deed can start with the free route.

Webster County also points owners to DeedWatch.com, described as a free service.

sections.h2: What else does the Recorder issue besides deed recordings?
sections.html:
Marriage licenses are a regular part of the counter work. Both parties must appear with valid government identification, and each person has to supply a Social Security number and the month and year any prior marriage ended. An online application is optional and speeds things up.

  • License fee: $53, cash only.
  • Certified copy: $9, the document used to change a name on a driver's license or Social Security card.
  • Validity: 30 days, and the ceremony must take place in Missouri.

The office also records and issues copies of DD-214 military discharge papers.

sections.h2: Which Webster County offices handle a home sale?
sections.html:
A sale touches several offices inside the same courthouse.

  • Recorder, Room 16: holds the deed, 417-859-5882.
  • Assessor, Room 19: values the parcel, 417-859-2169.
  • Collector, Room 15: bills and receives the tax, 417-859-2683.
  • County Clerk, Room 12: takes senior tax credit applications.

For an owner with a bill outstanding, the Collector's page has two firm rules. Delinquent years must be paid before the current year is accepted, and a statement is due on receipt and delinquent after December 31. A payment mailed on or before that day counts as on time if it carries a postmark.

sections.h2: What does Census data show about Webster County homes?
sections.html:
Webster County had an estimated 43,054 residents on July 1, 2025, up 10.1 percent from the April 2020 base of 39,087. The county counted 15,847 housing units, and owners occupy 77.4 percent of homes.

For 2020 to 2024 the median owned home was worth $228,800, with a typical monthly owner cost of $1,377 for those who carry a mortgage and $430 for those who do not. Median gross rent was $789. The average household had 2.82 people, and 82.1 percent of households had a broadband subscription.

Residents aged 65 and over are 17.0 percent of the population, compared with 33.3 percent in Stone County. Building permits numbered 226 in 2025.

sections.h2: How large is the Webster County economy?
sections.html:
Retail sales in Webster County reached $619.0 million in 2022, or $15,334 per resident, based on Census Bureau figures. Transportation and warehousing receipts were $67.6 million, health care and social assistance $54.1 million, and accommodation and food services $44.1 million.

About 58.5 percent of residents aged 16 and over are in the civilian labor force. Among adults 25 and older, 88.1 percent have a high school diploma and 18.3 percent hold a bachelor's degree. Another 8.1 percent of residents speak a language other than English at home, the highest share among Stone, Warren and Webster counties.

About 27.3 percent of residents are under 18, against 21.9 percent in Warren County and 16.7 percent in Stone County.

Median selected monthly owner costs and rent are listed above in the housing section, so a seller can compare an asking price with what local households pay each month.

sections.h2: What towns and schools are in Webster County?
sections.html:
Webster County covers 594 square miles of Ozarks upland and sits in the Springfield metropolitan area. The cities are Fordland, Marshfield, Niangua, Rogersville, Seymour and Strafford, and the one village is Diggins.

Public school districts include Fordland R-III, Logan-Rogersville R-VIII, Marshfield R-I, Niangua R-V and Seymour R-II. Students in some parts of the county attend Strafford and Fair Grove schools in Greene County or Conway in Laclede County. A property's district name appears on its tax statement and affects the rate.

faqs.q: What is the Webster County Recorder's phone number?
faqs.a: 417-859-5882. The office is in Room 16 of the courthouse in Marshfield and also takes email at recorder@webstercountymo.gov.

faqs.q: How much is the first page of a deed in Webster County?
faqs.a: $26 for the first page and $3 for each additional page, per the Recorder's page. A non-standard document adds $25. Confirm the total after the 2026 statewide $2 increase.

faqs.q: Is the Webster County online records search free?
faqs.a: There is a free level after registration, and in-office search in Room 16 is free. A paid plan costs $200 per month for 300 documents viewed or printed.

faqs.q: What margins does a Webster County deed need?
faqs.a: Three inches at the top of page one and three-quarters of an inch on the other sides, on 8.5 by 11 white paper.

faqs.q: How long is a Webster County marriage license valid?
faqs.a: Thirty days, and it must be used in Missouri. The license costs $53 in cash, and a certified copy is $9.
